events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.60)
events.body:
The trip is RydeX, a fixed-quote service: the fare was quoted upfront and mileage does not change it, so even though one off-route segment exists [F3] the detour km cannot be refunded — RD-2 routes non-metered cases to published add-ons only, and here there are none [F4][F6]. The billed distance equals the optimal route distance and there is no surge, waiting or extra item on the fare [F4][F5][F6], so the pure money question in RD-2 resolves to zero.

The trace settles the RD-4 branch against the driver: there is no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch, and the Central Expressway speed band alone does not exempt a segment [F11][F14][RD-4]. So F3 is not excused by a reasonable cause.

RD-5 is the live question. The driver proposed, before the segment, a specific routing — "go round via Balestier Road" — and the rider replied "Sure, your call." [F7][F8], both timestamped before the 08:37 segment start [F9][F3]. On its words this is not a general "whichever way is faster" authorisation and not a rider-named stop; it is a specific named road, and "your call" leaves the choice of the way to the driver within the proposal he made [F7][F8][RD-5]. But RD-5's named-road branch requires the record to tie the driven segment to the named road (a stop on it, a message placing the car on it, a road name in a fact); the fact table carries no road name for the driven path here [F3][G13]. Timing alone does not tie them, so the scope of the agreement over this segment cannot be read from the record — undetermined, not exempt and not counts.

That undetermined finding changes no amount, because the fare is fixed [F4][F6], but it does decide the account action: the driver has two upheld route disputes in the last 90 days [F17], so RD-6 would attach a flag if the segment were found non-exempt, and it would not if the segment were exempt. An element the record cannot settle that decides the flag means the case goes to a person rather than being ruled here [RD-6][G13].

Safety screen: I read every chat line and the complaint — the only messages are the driver's route proposal and the rider's agreement [F7][F8]; the driver's statement is a factual account of the same conversation [F10]. Nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses or alleges dangerous driving [F7][F8][F10]; the complaint is purely about the longer way round. Safety finding: none [RD-1].

Evidence: the chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F9], the GPS segment is measured [F3] and the fare components are itemised [F6], so the record settles the fare outcome; what it does not settle is the tie between the driven segment and the named road, which is the G13 gap and the reason for escalation rather than a ruling.
